policies.sourceText: All linguistics courses offered for the major must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher.

notes.text: Honors: Linguistics majors with a 3.50 GPA in the major may graduate with departmental honors by submitting and presenting a senior thesis. A written thesis proposal must be submitted to a sponsoring faculty member in the semester before the senior year. LIN 495 and LIN 496 (two semesters, six credits total) are taken in addition to the major's credits. Honors are recommended if the thesis is accepted and the student keeps a 3.50 GPA in linguistics courses.

TESOL teacher certification track (optional, not modeled as a requirement): Requires LIN 101, LIN 202 and/or LIN 203 with a grade of C or higher, an overall GPA of 3.0 and a GPA in the major of 3.0 for admission. The track adds LIN 307, LIN 405, LIN 431, five additional 3-credit linguistics courses (four upper-division), two years of language study, LIN 375 with LIN 449, LIN 378 with LIN 450, LIN 451, LIN 452, LIN 454, PSY 327, CEF 347, SSE 350 and LIN 344. Students must maintain a 3.0 GPA overall and in the major, and TESOL-certification courses may not be taken Grade/Pass/No Credit. Consult the Director of TESOL Teacher Preparation and the Undergraduate Program Director.

Five-Year Accelerated BA/MA in TESOL and Five-Year Accelerated BA/MAT in Linguistics and French, Italian, or Spanish are separate programs and are not modeled here. The BA/MA requires a 3.0 overall GPA and 3.3 in linguistics courses, an essay, two faculty recommendations, and interviews, and applications are due in the second semester of the sophomore year.
Many majors pursue a second major in a language or an adjacent field such as psychology or computer science. Students should consult the Director of Undergraduate Studies, Jenny Singleton.
LIN 405 satisfies the WRTD learning objective.
